labels.description: Adds litigation settlements, specifically the Rules Relief Class settlement described in Note 19, as a source of future limitations on Mastercard's rules and business practices; the legal proceedings note cross-reference also moves from Note 21 to Note 19.
labels.rationale: criterion 2: a new specific named proceeding (the Rules Relief Class settlement) is referenced as a source of business limitations; the Note 21 to Note 19 change alone would be a minor cross-reference update.

labels.description: No substantive change; the only difference is a page header/footer artifact (MASTERCARD 2025 FORM 10-K 31 PART I ITEM 1A. RISK FACTORS) captured at the end of the section.
labels.rationale: minor: the risk factor text is identical and the only change is a page layout artifact, which carries no change in substance.

labels.description: Adds a new disintermediation risk that payments industry participants may withhold rights to data Mastercard uses to power its solutions in order to support their own future solutions, potentially impairing the effectiveness of Mastercard's solutions.
labels.rationale: criterion 1: a new risk and data dependency (participants withholding data rights) is disclosed; the removed page footer is only a layout artifact.

labels.description: Rewords "grow our volume and/or services enough" to "grow our volume and/or services to the extent necessary" to offset higher incentives and pricing discounts, plus a page footer artifact.
labels.rationale: minor: the only textual change is stylistic rewording with identical meaning, and the remaining difference is a page layout artifact.

labels.description: Broadens the example technology from "cryptocurrency and blockchain" to "digital assets and blockchain" and adds that third parties Mastercard relies on for new technologies may fail to keep pace with changes "including with regard to AI", while trimming "safety and security technologies" to "security technologies".
labels.rationale: criterion 1 and criterion 3: a newly specified dependency on third parties keeping pace with AI is disclosed, and replacing cryptocurrency with the broader category of digital assets widens the scope of the technology risk.
